Subject: Follow-up: Redwood Dedicated sizing call & next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Alex/Priya — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: We validated that Nimbus is evaluating a private/dedicated deployment for clinical note generation and semantic search across patient records. Primary goals are predictable latency at 95th percentile < 200ms and support for 500 concurrent sessions with peak burst to ~1,200 QPS during batch runs.
- What we need next: a focused dedicated capacity sizing call (30-45m) with our solutions engineer to map those throughput/latency targets to GPU fleet sizing and recommended model/quantization profile.
- Proposed agenda: 1) confirm request pattern (QPS, prompt lengths, concurrency), 2) workload artifacts and KV/prefix cache opportunities, 3) sizing recommendation & cost ballpark, 4) next steps/PO timing.

I've attached our short sizing template to capture the workload numbers (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can fill the key fields before the call it will make the session much more productive.

Available slots this coming week: Tue 7/20 9:30-10:15 PT, Tue 7/20 10:30-11:15 PT, Wed 7/21 11:00-11:45 PT. If none of those work, send a few times that do and we'll accommodate.

Looping in Camila (CS) who will help coordinate logistics and Dylan (SE) who will join the sizing discussion.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Marissa Cole

Hi Alex — Dylan from Redwood SE team here, thanks for syncing with us. I'll run the sizing call and focus on mapping your QPS/concurrency to a recommended GPU pool, expected 95th/99th tail latency, and quantization/profile options. A few items that will make the call more actionable if you can share ahead of time:

- Expected sustained QPS and peak QPS (e.g., 500 sustained, 1,200 peak)
- Average and 95th percentile prompt lengths (tokens) for both generation and embedding pipelines
- Concurrency target (simultaneous sessions) and any per-customer isolation needs
- Tail-latency SLO (95th or 99th) and acceptable failure/fallback policy
- Whether you plan to pin a specific model (and which) or allow runtime switching/fallbacks

If you drop those into the attached XLSX we'll come to the call with two sizing options (cost-optimized vs. latency-optimized) and a recommended rollout plan. Looking forward to it.

—
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
